skill.name: antfu
skill.description: Apply Anthony Fu's opinionated web development preferences for TypeScript, pnpm, ESLint, Vue, Vite, Nuxt, and monorepos.
skill.summary: Opinionated TypeScript and web project setup guidance based on Anthony Fu's conventions.
skill.author: antfu

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, TypeScript examples, or protective ignore-file content. Confirmed risks are limited to mutable third-party GitHub Actions workflow recommendations and one global npm package installation instruction. No prompt injection or malicious data-exfiltration intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Reusable GitHub Actions workflows are pinned to mutable version tags.
remediation.suggestion: Pin sxzz/workflows references to reviewed commit SHAs, document trust assumptions, and review permissions before adoption.

remediation.issue: The release workflow delegates publishing to a third-party workflow with write and id-token permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Keep release permissions minimal, require maintainer review, and document that publishing workflows need explicit user approval.
Prefer a local devDependency or require explicit confirmation before running any global package installation command.

content.value_statement: Modern TypeScript projects need consistent choices for linting, testing, release, and documentation. This skill applies Anthony Fu's defaults for pnpm, ESLint, Vitest, Vue, Vite, Nuxt, and monorepos.
actual_capabilities: Recommends pnpm, named catalogs, and workspace layout for JavaScript and TypeScript projects.
Defines strict TypeScript and ESM defaults for package configuration.
Guides setup of @antfu/eslint-config for linting and formatting without Prettier.
Provides Vitest testing conventions, snapshot guidance, and package script examples.
Suggests Vue, Vite, Nuxt, UnoCSS, VitePress, and monorepo patterns from the included references.
Describes GitHub Actions workflow templates for autofix, tests, and library releases.
limitations: The guidance is opinionated and may not match every team standard.
It does not inspect a repository before recommending changes.
Some workflow examples depend on third-party reusable GitHub Actions.
Package installation and release steps still require user review and confirmation.

use_cases.title: Start a TypeScript Library
use_cases.description: Create a strict ESM package with pnpm, ESLint, Vitest, VitePress, and release scripts.

use_cases.title: Standardize a Vue App
use_cases.description: Apply Vue 3, Vite or Nuxt, UnoCSS, VueUse, and TypeScript component conventions.

use_cases.title: Organize a Monorepo
use_cases.description: Set up pnpm workspaces, shared scripts, ESLint cache, centralized aliases, and optional Turborepo guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Basic Defaults
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this project and recommend the smallest set of changes to match Anthony Fu's TypeScript, pnpm, ESM, and ESLint defaults.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Linting and Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Add quality tooling to an existing project
prompt_templates.prompt: Update the project plan for @antfu/eslint-config, Vitest, simple-git-hooks, and lint-staged. Include any package scripts that need user approval.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Vue Application Stack
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare Vite plus Vue and Nuxt for this application. Recommend the Anthony Fu style setup for state, props, emits, UnoCSS, and VueUse.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Monorepo Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration plan from a single package to a pnpm workspace monorepo with shared aliases, recursive scripts, ESLint cache, and release workflow safeguards.

output_examples.input: A new TypeScript package needs consistent tooling.
output_examples.output: A setup plan that selects pnpm, strict TypeScript, ESM, @antfu/eslint-config, Vitest, and VitePress documentation steps.

output_examples.input: A Vue app needs framework and style guidance.
output_examples.output: A recommendation that chooses Vite or Nuxt by use case and applies Vue 3 Composition API, shallow refs, UnoCSS, and VueUse.

output_examples.input: A team wants shared conventions across packages.
output_examples.output: A monorepo checklist covering pnpm workspaces, package scripts, ESLint cache, centralized aliases, and release workflow review points.

best_practices: Ask before running package manager, lint fix, release, or global install commands.
Review third-party workflow permissions before adding GitHub Actions examples.
Apply the conventions incrementally when a repository already has established tooling.
anti_patterns: Do not replace working team standards only because the skill prefers another tool.
Do not run release or publish steps without maintainer approval.
Do not add third-party reusable workflows without pinning and permission review.

faq.question: What projects is this skill best for?
faq.answer: It is best for TypeScript, Vue, Vite, Nuxt, library, and monorepo projects that want Anthony Fu style conventions.

faq.question: Does it replace Prettier?
faq.answer: The skill recommends @antfu/eslint-config for formatting and linting, so Prettier is usually not needed.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. Users should approve package installation, lint fixes, and release commands.

faq.question: Are the GitHub Actions examples safe?
faq.answer: They use third-party reusable workflows. Review the workflow source, pin commits, and check permissions before adoption.

faq.question: Can teams customize these defaults?
faq.answer: Yes. The conventions are opinionated, but teams can adapt catalogs, scripts, workflows, and framework choices.
